title: French students and unions protest school conditions nationwide

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against crumbling schools, teacher shortages, overcrowded classes, and underfunding from austerity budgets.
tea.want: They demand better investment in schools, more teachers, and funding for education instead of state repression.
tea.changed: Oct 14: Nationwide demonstrations entered their fourth week, with more than 160,000 turning out across the country.

summary: High-school students, university students, teachers, parents, and trade unions have staged nationwide protests in France over deteriorating school conditions, chronic underfunding, and teacher shortages. Demonstrations, blockades, and marches have been organized across cities including Saint-Denis, Paris, Lyon, Lille, Marseille, and Nantes. Participants demand increased state investment in crumbling educational infrastructure and more teaching staff. According to reports, the demonstrations have faced a heavy state response, with riot police deploying tear gas during marches, prompting lawyers to form protective human chains around teenagers in Saint-Denis.
demands: More teachers to combat overcrowding and burnout
State funding for education instead of police repression
Greater equality in funding outside central cities
response: According to Daily Mail, riot police fired tear gas at marches in Nantes and near the Montparnasse area of Paris during nationwide demonstrations.

crowd.text: More than 160,000 schoolchildren and trade unionists turned out across the country on Tuesday

updates.text: High-school student blockades and protests spread from Saint-Denis to universities, drawing in teachers and parents.
Nationwide demonstrations entered their fourth week with over 160,000 participants and clashes involving riot police.
